svg.title: Distinguish co-occurrence from a transmitted allele
svg.desc: An affected XᵃY father and a possible carrier XᴬXᵃ mother can have an affected XᵃY son. Two labelled arrows explicitly route paternal Y and maternal Xᵃ into the son. The father does not transmit his X to that son. Therefore observing an affected father and son does not by itself exclude X-linked recessive inheritance. This is one possible genotype assignment, not proof of the mother’s genotype from a pair of phenotypes. Y-linked and autosomal alternatives need full-family and genotype checks with stated penetrance, mutation and record assumptions.

g.text: Distinguish co-occurrence from a transmitted allele
A possible family model tests a shortcut rather than diagnosing a real pedigree.
Observed: an affected father and an affected son. Co-occurrence is not proof of direct allele transfer.
Test an X-linked recessive explanation with explicit alleles and a possible carrier mother:
The father’s X goes to daughters, not this son. The mother can supply the son’s Xᵃ.
Y-linked and autosomal alternatives require their own full-family checks; male-only is insufficient.
A model excluding an affected child must state penetrance, mutation and recording assumptions.
